column1: mysql CLI — run one statement without entering the `mysql>` prompt? (and which flag belongs to `mysql` vs `docker`)
mysql CLI — why does `-pPASS` warn "Using a password on the command line ... can be insecure", and the clean fix?
column2:
The literal password on the command line is visible to other users via the
process table (ps -ef) and lands in shell history. In a throwaway dev container
it's low-stakes — safe to ignore.

Clean fix: put it in ~/.my.cnf so the flag disappears —
  [client]
  password=...
then  chmod 600 ~/.my.cnf   (owner-only, or the client refuses to use it)

column1: `docker compose exec` — what does `-T` do, and when do you need it?
column2:
-T disables the pseudo-TTY that exec allocates by default. That default TTY
fights a redirected/piped stdin -> "the input device is not a TTY", or the input
is silently unread.

Rule: piping/redirecting a file IN -> use -T; wanting the interactive prompt -> omit it.

  docker compose exec -T mysql mysql -u root -p db < schema.sql   # -T (piped file)
  docker compose exec    mysql mysql -u root -p db                # no -T (interactive)

column1: Wayland — copy a file's contents to the clipboard from the shell (and read it back)?
column2:
wl-clipboard provides wl-copy / wl-paste (Wayland; KDE Plasma).

  wl-copy < file.txt      # reads stdin -> clipboard (the < feeds the file in)
  wl-paste                # prints clipboard to stdout
  wl-paste > out.txt      # dump clipboard into a file
  wl-copy --primary       # target the middle-click "primary" selection instead

(To DUPLICATE a file rather than grab its text, that's just:  cp src dst)
